Sub-sector: Industrial energy efficiency; Building energy efficiency
Domestic instrument name: 合同能源管理项目增值税优惠
English instrument name: VAT incentive for energy performance contracting projects
Description: Under Cai Shui [2010] No. 110, China has granted VAT preferences since 1 January 2011 to qualifying energy service companies (ESCOs) implementing energy performance contracting (EPC) projects: (1) VAT-taxable goods within the project transferred to the energy-using enterprise are temporarily exempted from VAT (the goods component); (2) revenue from EPC services is exempted from VAT (the services component, later continued under Cai Shui [2016] No. 36, Annex 3, Article 27, Item (1)). The policy encourages ESCOs to implement energy-saving retrofits for industrial enterprises and building owners through the EPC model. After the VAT Law of the People's Republic of China took effect on 1 January 2026, MOFSTA Announcement [2026] No. 10 repealed the above VAT exemption provisions, and the preference terminated on 31 December 2025. The CIT "three-year exemption, three-year half reduction" preference is unaffected and remains in force.
Last revisions (Details): The VAT Law of the People's Republic of China took effect on 1 January 2026. MOFSTA Announcement [2026] No. 10 repealed Article 1 of Cai Shui [2010] No. 110 (the VAT exemption provision) and the VAT exemption for EPC services under Cai Shui [2016] No. 36, Annex 3, Article 27, Item (1). From 1 January 2026, EPC services are again subject to VAT (6% for technical services, 13% for equipment sales). No special transitional arrangement applies to existing contracts. The CIT preference (three-year exemption, three-year half reduction) is unaffected.
Administrating authorities: Ministry of Finance (responsible for VAT policy formulation); State Taxation Administration (responsible for VAT collection and administration); National Development and Reform Commission (responsible for energy performance contracting and energy service industry policy)
Asset: Buildings energy systems (electricity systems, heating systems, etc.); Industrial plants
Asset (Details): Energy-saving retrofit equipment covered by EPC projects, including high-efficiency lighting systems, high-efficiency air-conditioning systems, high-efficiency boilers and thermal systems, motor system energy saving, waste heat and pressure utilisation, energy-saving retrofits of building envelopes, etc. VAT-taxable goods (equipment) transferred by the ESCO to the energy-using enterprise are subject to the temporary VAT exemption.
Agent (Detail): Qualified energy service companies (ESCOs) are the implementers of EPC projects and the beneficiaries of the VAT preference. Energy-using enterprises (industrial enterprises, building owners, etc.) are the project clients and purchasers of the energy-saving benefits. Project implementation requires an energy management contract (energy-saving benefit-sharing type).
Activity: Production, generation or conversion; Purchase or use
Activity (Details): ESCOs provide one-stop EPC services to energy-using enterprises, including energy-saving diagnosis, scheme design, equipment procurement and installation, and operation and maintenance. Energy-using enterprises reduce energy consumption and carbon emissions through energy-saving retrofits. The VAT preference lowers the tax cost of ESCOs, indirectly reducing the end-user price of energy-saving services.
Intensity (Details): Goods transfer (equipment): temporarily exempted from VAT (100% relief; previously subject to a 13% rate). Service revenue (energy-saving diagnosis, operation and maintenance management): exempted from VAT (100% relief; previously subject to a 6% rate). The preference terminated on 31 December 2025 upon implementation of the VAT Law.
Requirement specification: The ESCO must simultaneously satisfy: (1) registered in China with independent legal-person status; (2) implementing EPC projects (energy-saving benefit-sharing type); (3) compliance with the General Technical Rules for Energy Performance Contracting (GB/T 24915-2010); (4) no affiliated relationship between the ESCO and the energy-using enterprise; (5) independent accounting for the project.
Legal statute: Cai Shui [2010] No. 110, Notice on VAT, Business Tax and Enterprise Income Tax Policies for Promoting the Development of the Energy Service Industry; Cai Shui [2016] No. 36, Annex 3; MOFSTA Announcement [2026] No. 10, Announcement on Matters Concerning the Continuity of VAT Preferential Policies After the Implementation of the VAT Law
